title: Chapter 2 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of filesystem navigation, listing, and path magic!

questions.question: What does the root directory contain?
questions.explanation: The root (`/`) is the top of the filesystem tree, containing all other directories and files.

questions.question: Which command prints your current working directory?
questions.explanation: `pwd` (Print Working Directory) shows where you are.

questions.question: What does `cd ..` do?
questions.explanation: `..` always represents the parent directory (one level up).

questions.question: How do you go to your home directory instantly?
questions.explanation: Both `cd` alone and `cd ~` take you home.

questions.question: Which `ls` flag shows hidden files?
questions.explanation: `-a` includes all files, even those starting with a dot.

questions.question: Which `ls` flag displays file sizes in a human‑readable format like 1K, 5M?
questions.explanation: `-h` stands for human‑readable, best used with `-l`.

questions.question: What does `mkdir -p projects/cybron/app` do?
questions.explanation: `-p` creates parent directories as needed, preventing errors.

questions.question: The command `rmdir` can delete a directory that is not empty.
questions.explanation: `rmdir` only removes empty directories. Use `rm -r` for non‑empty ones.

questions.question: What is the danger of `rm -rf /`?
options: It removes all files in the system if run as root
questions.explanation: `rm -rf` deletes everything recursively and forcefully. As root, it can destroy the OS.

questions.question: What does the glob pattern `*.txt` match?
options: Files with 'txt' anywhere in the name
questions.explanation: `*` expands to any string, so `*.txt` matches anything that ends with `.txt`.

questions.question: How would you list all files that start with 'a' followed by exactly one character?
questions.explanation: `?` matches exactly one character, so `a?` matches 'a' then one character.

questions.question: Which character class matches any single digit?
questions.explanation: Brackets with a range `[0-9]` match any digit 0 through 9.

questions.question: What does `ls -R` do?
questions.explanation: `-R` (recursive) dives into subdirectories and lists their contents too.

questions.question: If you are in `/var/log`, what does `cd /home` do?
options: Goes to /home using an absolute path
questions.explanation: Paths starting with `/` are absolute, so it takes you directly there.

questions.question: What does `cd -` do?
questions.explanation: `cd -` changes to the last directory you were in.

questions.question: How can you safely test which files a glob would match?
options: Use echo followed by the glob
questions.explanation: `echo *.txt` prints the expanded list, showing exactly what files will be used.

questions.question: What command would create three directories (docs, src, bin) in one line?
questions.explanation: `mkdir` accepts multiple arguments, creating all specified directories.

questions.question: A file named `.bashrc` is hidden by default.
questions.explanation: Files and directories starting with a dot are hidden from normal `ls` output.

questions.question: Which `ls` option sorts files by modification time, newest first?
questions.explanation: `-t` sorts by time. Combine with `-r` to reverse (oldest first).

questions.question: What does the `.` symbol represent in a path?
questions.explanation: `.` is the current working directory.
